about: ESR Group is a pan-Asia-Pacific logistics real estate developer, owner and fund manager based in Singapore (with Hong Kong operations), with a portfolio of warehouses and data centers and fund management of over $150bn of assets. Customers are e-commerce, retail and logistics tenants, and income comes from rent, development and fees. Taken private in 2025 by a consortium including Starwood Capital, Warburg Pincus and Sixth Street, after Hong Kong listing (1821). B2B property, no consumer profile.

International Distribution Services is the parent of Royal Mail and General Logistics Systems (GLS), a London-based postal and parcel group delivering letters and parcels in the UK and across Europe and Canada. It had revenue over GBP 12bn and about 140,000 employees. In 2025 it was acquired by Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky's EP Group for about GBP 3.6bn and delisted from the London Stock Exchange. Royal Mail is a very well-known UK consumer brand.

wiki.title: International Distribution Services
wiki.text: International Distribution Services Limited is a British company providing postal and courier services. IDS was created in 2013 by the UK government as a new holding company of Royal Mail, and a majority of its shares were then sold on the London Stock Exchange, with the government initially retaining a 30 per cent at the time. As of April 2025, IDS is owned and operated by Czech-based EP Group, owned by Daniel Křetínský.

about: BigBasket is a Bengaluru-based Indian online grocery and supermarket business offering scheduled and quick delivery of fruit, vegetables, groceries and household goods in more than 25 Indian cities. Tata Digital bought a majority stake in 2021 and it is part of the Tata Group, with Alibaba and Abraaj as earlier investors. Revenue is around INR 100bn. Private. Strong urban consumer brand in India with substantial advertising.

Aramex is a Dubai-based logistics and express delivery company founded in 1982, offering courier, freight forwarding, warehousing and e-commerce fulfilment across the Middle East, Africa, Asia and beyond. Customers are businesses and online shoppers. Revenue is about 1.5 billion dollars, with an AED 2 billion funding figure reported in the input. Listed on the Dubai Financial Market (ARMX); Abu Dhabi's Abu Dhabi Ports (AD Ports) became majority owner of Aramex in 2025. Visible brand in the Gulf.

wiki.title: Aramex
wiki.text: Aramex is an Emirati multinational logistics, courier and package delivery company based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. The company was founded by Fadi Ghandour and Bill Kingson in 1982 in Amman, Jordan.

about: Agility is a Dubai-based logistics and supply chain group, with roots in Kuwait (Agility Public Warehousing), that provides freight forwarding, warehousing, industrial parks, and infrastructure services and owns Menzies Aviation stakes and Tristar. Customers are businesses and governments across the Middle East, Asia and Africa. It has reported funding of about $2.5 billion. B2B, little consumer brand awareness.

about: Global Partners LP is a Waltham, Massachusetts-based master limited partnership (NYSE: GLP) that stores, distributes and markets petroleum products, renewable fuels, natural gas and propane, and operates convenience stores and gas stations (Alltown, Sunoco-branded sites) in the Northeast and mid-Atlantic. Revenue is around $17 billion. Customers are wholesale, commercial and retail fuel customers. Consumer-facing via its gas stations, but little corporate brand awareness.

Stord is a US commerce enablement company that provides fulfilment, warehousing, freight and software for e-commerce and consumer brands, with a national network of warehouses and a cloud platform for inventory and order management. Headquartered in Atlanta, it was founded in 2015 and has raised several hundred million dollars from venture investors. Customers are direct-to-consumer and retail brands. B2B logistics technology with little public brand awareness.

about: Detroit Manufacturing Systems is a Detroit, Michigan automotive manufacturing and logistics company. According to the input it works in automotive manufacturing and logistics-related services. Customers, products, ownership and scale are not confirmed here, and it should be checked carefully since similar names exist. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Archion is a Japanese commercial vehicle holding company formed to combine truck makers Hino Motors and Mitsubishi Fuso Truck and Bus, bringing together Toyota and Daimler Truck interests in the Japanese and Asian truck market. Headquartered in Tokyo. Customers are logistics firms, fleet operators and governments buying trucks and buses. Planned as a listed company on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. B2B brand, familiar through the Hino and Fuso names rather than Archion itself.

about: Tristar Transport, part of Tristar Group, is a Dubai-based logistics company specialising in the transport and storage of bulk liquids such as fuel, chemicals and lubricants by road, sea and terminals across the Middle East, Africa and Asia. Customers are oil and gas, chemicals and industrial firms, with revenue from transport, storage and fuel services. Crunchbase shows about $1.1 billion in funding, likely debt and investment. Privately held. B2B, little consumer awareness.

UTM Offshore is a Nigerian marine logistics and offshore vessel business based in Abuja, serving oil and gas companies. Funding of about $2 billion is shown. B2B with no consumer awareness. It operates vessels and offshore support services, including supply and crew boats, for Nigerian oil operators. Not a consumer-facing brand. The input lists energy, logistics and oil and gas categories, plus $2 billion of funding. Fleet size and clients are not given.

about: Emergent Cold Latin America is a Dallas-based cold storage and logistics operator in Latin America, with $1.2 billion funding shown. B2B logistics business with no consumer visibility. Operates temperature-controlled warehouses and distribution in Latin America such as Mexico and Chile. Customers include food producers and retailers. The input shows total funding of about $1.2 billion, but the company's sites and brands are not detailed.

about: Milan-based Italian rail and transport group FNM, operating Lombardy regional rail via Trenord and Malpensa Express, as well as infrastructure. Owned by the Lombardy region. Consumer brand in Lombardy. Concession and rail operations include the Malpensa Express. Listed on Borsa Italiana and part-owned by the Lombardy Region. FNM also owns stakes in airports and bus operations, and the company is listed on the Milan stock exchange.

Norfolk Southern Corporation is one of the largest US freight railroads, operating about 19,000 route miles in 22 states and Washington DC, and serving most major eastern ports. It carries intermodal, coal, automotive, chemicals, agricultural and industrial goods for shippers. Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, it has around 20,000 employees and revenue of roughly 12 billion dollars. Listed on the NYSE (NSC). Union Pacific announced a plan to acquire it in 2025. Known for the 2023 East Palestine derailment. B2B transport brand with moderate public recognition in the eastern US.

American Bath Group is an Irving, Texas manufacturer of bathroom products, including bathtubs, showers and related fixtures under brands such as Aquatic and Lasco Bathware, selling to home improvement chains, builders and distributors in North America. It is privately held, and Crunchbase shows funding of about $2.3 billion. B2B supplier, mostly sold through retail partners, with low consumer brand awareness. Details of ownership were not confirmed.

about: Denver-based construction materials company producing aggregates, cement and ready-mix concrete across the US and British Columbia. Founded in 2009 and listed on the NYSE (SUM), it bought Argos USA's cement business in 2024. Agreed in 2025 to be acquired by Quikrete Holdings. Customers are contractors and public infrastructure agencies. B2B brand.

Doman Building Materials Group is a Vancouver-based wholesale distributor of building materials, including lumber, treated wood, plywood and specialty products, serving home improvement retailers and contractors across Canada and the US. It merged with CanWel Building Materials Group (TSX: CWX) in 2019 to form a larger Canadian distributor. B2B distribution with no consumer profile.

about: Crux AI is a Palo Alto, California company in the AI infrastructure sector; the Crunchbase description says it provides integrated AI services. Crunchbase shows very large total funding of about $27 billion, with the latest round dated September 2026, which would place it among the most heavily funded private AI infrastructure businesses. Customers and revenue model are not clear from the data available, though they are likely enterprise and AI developers. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Firmus Technologies is an Australian company building AI data centers it calls AI Factories, using liquid-cooled infrastructure to host GPU compute for AI developers and enterprises, with its Project Southgate and Tasmanian sites linked to Nvidia-based capacity. Crunchbase lists headquarters in Saint Leonards, Tasmania, and about $13.1 billion in total funding, latest dated August 2026. Private B2B infrastructure business with limited public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Cerebras Systems is a Sunnyvale, California AI chip and systems company, founded in 2016, known for its Wafer-Scale Engine, a very large processor, and the CS-series systems. It sells AI hardware and cloud inference services to enterprises, research labs, governments and sovereign AI customers, with partners such as G42. Crunchbase shows about $4.7 billion in total funding. Went through a long IPO process. B2B, with limited consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Cerebras Systems
wiki.text: Cerebras Systems Inc., headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, develops semiconductors, supercomputers, and related software to power artificial intelligence deep-learning applications such as inference engines. Products include its wafer scale engine (WSE)-3 semiconductors, its CS-3 supercomputers, and its "AI inference cloud" and "AI training cloud" APIs, which allow users to access the company's computing power without buying its hardware. The company also builds data centers using its processors and supercomputers to provide cloud computing services directly to clients.

about: Lambda is a San Francisco GPU cloud and AI infrastructure company, founded in 2012, offering on-demand and reserved NVIDIA GPU clusters, workstations and servers to AI researchers, startups and enterprises, and building large AI factories, with Microsoft and Nvidia deals. Crunchbase shows about $6.1 billion in total funding. It has pursued an IPO. B2B tech brand, well known among AI developers and with little public consumer awareness.

Diamond Infrastructure Solutions is a Houston, Texas infrastructure company focusing on operational infrastructure, per Crunchbase, with recorded funding of about $2.9 billion. It could be linked to a pipeline or energy infrastructure business, but the input has no detail on assets, customers or ownership. It is likely a B2B infrastructure company with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Baseten is a San Francisco AI infrastructure startup, founded in 2019, that provides an inference platform for deploying and serving machine learning models in production for developers and enterprises. Revenue comes from usage-based compute and platform fees. Customers include AI-native startups and larger companies running generative AI models. It has raised large venture rounds from investors such as IVP, Spark and Greylock, with total funding of about $2.1 billion per Crunchbase. B2B developer brand with little public awareness.

Biren Technology is a Shanghai-based AI chip startup that designs high-performance general-purpose GPUs for AI training and inference in data centres, with its BR100 series. Customers are Chinese cloud, internet and enterprise AI buyers. Founded in 2019, it has raised about $1.7 billion in funding and faces US export-control constraints on advanced chip manufacturing. Listed in Hong Kong in early 2026. B2B semiconductor firm with no consumer brand awareness.

about: SambaNova is a US AI hardware and software company, founded in 2017 in Palo Alto and based in San Jose, California, that sells reconfigurable dataflow chips (SN40L) and a full-stack platform and cloud service for running large AI models, with a focus on fast inference. Customers are enterprises, governments and national labs. It has raised about $1.1 billion from SoftBank, Intel Capital and others, with total shown near $2.5 billion. B2B with limited public awareness.

wiki.title: SambaNova
wiki.text: SambaNova is an American artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor hardware company. The company designs and manufactures hardware accelerators termed Reconfigurable Dataflow Units (RDUs) adjusted for deep learning models and generative AI applications.

about: Ayar Labs is a San Jose startup developing optical I/O chiplets using silicon photonics, which move data between processors with light for AI and high performance computing systems. Customers include chipmakers and hyperscalers, and it has partnered with Nvidia, Intel and GlobalFoundries. Founded in 2015, it has raised about 370 million dollars. B2B semiconductor deep tech, no consumer awareness. Revenue is early-stage and comes from development contracts and product evaluations. The brand is known in the semiconductor and AI hardware industry, and not to consumers.
